what_its_for: Aminolevulinic acid is used in two main ways: (1) As a solution applied to the skin to treat rough, scaly skin patches called actinic keratoses (precancerous spots caused by sun damage) using a special blue light treatment. (2) As a drink taken before brain tumor surgery to help surgeons see and remove cancerous brain tissue more clearly under a special blue-violet light.
how_to_take: FOR SKIN TREATMENT (Levulan Kerastick / Ameluz): A healthcare provider will apply this medicine directly to the affected skin patches in their office. You will then sit under a special blue light for a set amount of time. Do not apply this medicine yourself unless specifically instructed. FOR BRAIN SURGERY (Gleolan): You will drink this medicine mixed in water about 2 to 4 hours before your surgery begins. Your doctor or nurse will prepare and give you the drink. Do not eat or drink anything else for at least 2 hours before taking it.
dosing: FOR SKIN TREATMENT: Your doctor will determine how much to apply based on the size and number of skin patches. Treatment is typically done once per session in a clinic. FOR BRAIN SURGERY (Gleolan): The usual dose is 20 mg per kilogram of body weight, taken as a single drink before surgery. Your healthcare team will calculate and prepare the exact dose for you.
missed_dose: FOR SKIN TREATMENT: If you miss your scheduled clinic appointment, call your doctor's office as soon as possible to reschedule. FOR BRAIN SURGERY: Since this is given once before a scheduled surgery, if you forget to take it or had trouble taking it, tell your surgical team right away before your procedure begins so they can make the necessary adjustments.
storage: FOR SKIN TREATMENT (Levulan Kerastick): Store at room temperature, away from heat and light. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children. FOR BRAIN SURGERY (Gleolan): This medicine is stored and prepared by hospital staff. You do not need to store it at home. Once mixed with water, it should be used within 24 hours.
what_to_avoid: SUNLIGHT AND BRIGHT LIGHT: After skin treatment, avoid sunlight, bright indoor lights, and tanning beds for at least 40 hours, as your treated skin will be extremely sensitive to light and can burn severely. Wear protective clothing and stay indoors as much as possible. After taking Gleolan before surgery, avoid bright light exposure to your skin and eyes until after the procedure. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery after taking Gleolan, as it may affect your ability to react. Avoid alcohol before and around the time of treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially antibiotics, diuretics (water pills), or any other medicines that increase sun sensitivity.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe skin redness, blistering, swelling, or pain at the treated area after skin treatment; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or dizziness; nausea, vomiting, or low blood pressure after taking Gleolan; unusual skin reactions or burns after light exposure; chest pain or fast heartbeat; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you after treatment.
when_it_works: FOR SKIN TREATMENT: After the light treatment session, treated skin patches may become red, swollen, and crusty over the following days — this is normal and means the treatment is working. Skin usually heals over 2 to 4 weeks. Your doctor will check at a follow-up visit to see how well the precancerous patches responded. FOR BRAIN SURGERY: The medicine works during surgery by making cancerous brain tissue glow pink or red under the special light, helping your surgeon see exactly where the tumor is. You will not notice this yourself.
special_populations: PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully established. CHILDREN: Gleolan is not approved for use in children under 18 years old for brain surgery. Skin treatment products are generally used in adults only. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your doctor may need to adjust your treatment. PORPHYRIA: Do not use aminolevulinic acid if you have a condition called porphyria (a rare blood disorder) or known sensitivity to porphyrins, as this medicine may cause serious harm. ELDERLY PATIENTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects; close monitoring by a healthcare provider is recommended.
